en: Title: Niraupamyastava (Hymn to the Peerless One) Author: Nāgārjuna Source: Tola & Dragonetti, 1985, pp. 12–14 Homage to the Buddha! O you who are peerless, whose nature is beyond comparison, To you, the peerless one, I offer praise. O you who have abandoned all conceptual proliferation, Whose mind is free from the stains of attachment and aversion, To you, the peerless one, I offer praise. O you who have transcended the world with its gods, humans, and asuras, Who have reached the further shore of the ocean of existence, To you, the peerless one, I offer praise. O you who are the light that dispels the darkness of ignorance, The sun that dries up the ocean of suffering, To you, the peerless one, I offer praise. O you who are the medicine for the disease of the three poisons, The physician who heals the ailments of sentient beings, To you, the peerless one, I offer praise. O you who are the refuge for those wandering in the wilderness of saṃsāra, The protector of the unprotected, the friend of the friendless, To you, the peerless one, I offer praise. O you who have realized the truth of dependent origination, For whom there is no self, no being, no life-principle, To you, the peerless one, I offer praise. O you who have taught the path of peace and liberation, The noble eightfold path leading to the cessation of suffering, To you, the peerless one, I offer praise. Thus, with a mind full of devotion, I have praised The peerless one, the supreme among all beings. By this merit, may all sentient beings Attain the state of the peerless Buddha.
Homage to you, O Peerless One, who understands the meaning of the absence of intrinsic nature!
You, who are intent on the welfare of this world ruined by false views—
nothing at all has indeed been seen by you with the Buddha-eye;
yet your vision, O Protector, is unsurpassed, perceiving the reality of the ultimate truth.
From the perspective of ultimate reality, there is neither a knower nor anything to be known here;
oh, how you have awakened to the nature of phenomena (dharmatā), which is so exceedingly difficult to understand!
No phenomenon whatsoever has been produced by you, nor has any been ceased.
The unsurpassed state was attained precisely through the vision of equality.
You did not seek nirvāṇa by means of withdrawing from saṃsāra;
O Protector, you have realized peace because saṃsāra is not apprehended.
You have realized the single flavor of both affliction and purification;
because the realm of phenomena (dharmadhātu) is indivisible, you are pure in every respect.
O Lord, not even a single syllable has been uttered by you.
The entire assembly of those to be trained has been satisfied by the rain of Dharma.
You have no attachment to the aggregates, the elements, or the sense-bases;
with a mind like space, you are independent of all phenomena.
O Protector, the notion of a "sentient being" does not arise for you in any way whatsoever;
yet, toward sentient beings afflicted by suffering, you are exceedingly compassionate in nature.
O Lord, regarding pleasure and pain, self and non-self, permanence and impermanence, and so forth—
Thus, your intellect does not cling to various conceptual constructions.
Your understanding is that there is no going or coming whatsoever among phenomena;
because there is no state of being a heap anywhere, you are a knower of the ultimate truth.

O Noble One: You possess the nature of the totality; therefore, you are a knower of the ultimate truth, you are all-pervading, and yet you are not born anywhere. (Alternatively: you have transcended birth.)
O Great Sage, you are inconceivable in terms of birth, nature, and body.
The world is devoid of oneness and multiplicity, resembling an echo;
[according to the testimony of Candrakīrti: it is devoid of identity and difference].
O blameless one, you have realized that which is free from transition and destruction;
it is devoid of permanence and annihilation, and is stripped of both the characterized and the characteristics.
O Lord, you have realized that saṃsāra is like a dream or an illusion;
O sinless one, you have conquered the afflictions along with their very root, the latent tendencies,
and through the very nature of those afflictions, you have attained the deathless state.
O steadfast one, you have seen the formless form as if it were possessed of form;
yet, though your limbs shine with the primary marks, you appear within the sphere of form.
And by the sight of this form, you are not said to be "seen."

When the Dharma is seen, you are well-seen; yet the true nature of phenomena (dharmatā) is not seen. Furthermore: through the vision of the Dharma, there is no hollowness in your body, nor is there flesh, bone, or blood.
You displayed a body in the sky like a rainbow;
there was no disease or impurity in your body, nor was there any arising of hunger or thirst.
You demonstrated worldly activity only for the sake of conforming to the ways of the world.
O Sinless One, you have no fault of karmic obstruction whatsoever;
for the sake of compassion for the world, you have demonstrated the transcendence of karma.
O Lord, because there is no differentiation in the realm of phenomena (*dharmadhātu*), there is no differentiation of vehicles.
The three vehicles were proclaimed by you for the sake of introducing sentient beings [to the path].
O Jina, your body is eternal, stable, and auspicious, consisting of the Dharma;
yet, for the sake of those to be trained, you have displayed your passing into nirvāṇa.
Furthermore, in immeasurable world-systems, you are beheld by those devoted to you who long for your passing away,
birth, perfect enlightenment, turning of the wheel [of Dharma], and parinirvāṇa. O Protector, you have no conceit, no conceptual construction, and no movement.

"Your Buddha-activity proceeds in the world without effort. (24) Thus, having scattered flowers of virtues over the Sugata— who is inconceivable and immeasurable— whatever merit I have obtained, [may it be for the welfare of all beings].
By this, may sentient beings here become partakers of the most profound Dharma of the Lord of Munis.
Thus ends the *Niraupamya-stava*.
